thread:
Alex Chen: Heads up — noticed a big compile surge and KV eviction spike after yesterday's heuristic merge (PR #4321). Tail latency on small-batch short-seq jobs jumped ~3-4x.
perf-ci-bot: CI perf alert: builds failing perf threshold on models/case-shortseq (https://ci.internal/redwood/4321)
Priya Nair: ugh, saw the alert. Is this the new entropy-based kernel ranking you merged?
Miguel Santos: I started a quick bisect, looks like the heuristic change at commit 9f2c3b7 touches kernel_score.py which picks between fused-gemm and nv-optimized kernels.
Jo Park: Can you paste the failing CI snippet?
perf-ci-bot: ``
FAILED: latency > threshold (p95 220ms vs baseline 65ms)
Compile storms observed: 120 compilations/min on pool-4
KV cache churn: evictions/sec jumped 8x
``
Priya Nair: Local repro: same pattern. The new score function prefers the variant with lower static cost but higher codegen variance — causes repeated recompiles for slightly different shapes. KV TTLs are getting invalidated because cache keys include kernel fingerprints that keep changing.
Samir Patel: Is this causing rollout blockers? I see a few customer routes pegging error budgets.
Alex Chen: Yes, we put the release on hold. @deploy-bot pls pause rollout for group:shortseq.
deploy-bot: Rollout paused for group:shortseq per request by Alex Chen.
Miguel Santos: Bisect narrowed to 9f2c3b7 -> 9f2c3b7^ (the heuristic tweak). Reverting that change locally returns perf to baseline.
Priya Nair: Quick mitigation idea: add a fingerprint-stabilizer that rounds kernel selection for small batches and short seqs, or fallback to last-known-good kernel when compile rate > X.
Jo Park: Agree. Also we should stop including transient codegen flags in KV cache keys until we stabilize selection.
Samir Patel: Can we hotfix the scorer to prefer stable picks for windows with high cache churn? If yes, we can unfreeze rollout after hotfix and monitor.
Miguel Santos: I'll open a hotfix PR with the stable-pick guard and an integration test to assert compile-rate < 10/min for the shortseq workload. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4387
Priya Nair: Running perf profile now and posting flamegraph: https://artifacts.redwood/fg/1977654321-shortseq.svg
Alex Chen: Nice. Flamegraph shows most time in JIT reconciliation and codegen, not execution.
perf-ci-bot: CI run for hotfix PR 4387 queued. Will report perf metrics when done.
Jo Park: If CI confirms fix, let's do staged unfreeze (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with rollbacks on any perf bump. Add an alert for compile-rate > 20/min.
Samir Patel: Documenting rollback plan and owning postmortem. Priya, can you draft a short incident note with root cause and planned QA?
Priya Nair: On it. I'll include reproducer steps, the bisect commit, and the KV key audit checklist.
Alex Chen: Thanks team. Good catch on the finger-printing surface area. We'll follow up in eng-runtime retrospective. :thumbsup:
